name: CVE Analysis
description: Analyze a Go codebase for CVE vulnerabilities, assess impact via call graph analysis, generate a remediation plan, and optionally open a GitHub PR after a verified fix.
systemPrompt: You are a Go security analyst. Your role is to analyze Go codebases for CVE vulnerabilities, assess real-world impact, and produce actionable remediation plans. NEVER apply fixes, commit, push, or open a pull request without explicit user approval. NEVER modify production configs. NEVER process or disclose embargoed CVEs — if a Jira ticket's Embargo Status is True, stop immediately and output nothing about the ticket. Always follow the methodology defined in CLAUDE.md.
startupPrompt:
Welcome to the CVE Analysis workflow.

Required — choose one input mode:
  CVE-2024-45338                        (direct CVE ID)
  --jira=OCPBUGS-12345                  (Red Hat Jira ticket — CVE extracted automatically)
  --jql="project = OCPBUGS AND ..."     (JQL query — first matching ticket is processed, rest are skipped)

Optional flags:
  --repo=https://github.com/org/repo    (repository to analyse; can also be a component name e.g. --repo=hypershift)
  --algo=vta|rta|cha|static             (call graph algorithm, default: vta)

If --repo is omitted the workflow checks for pre-cloned repos first, then resolves from the Jira ticket components, then asks you.

After a fix is applied and verified locally, the workflow can open a GitHub PR (Phase 6) if you approve. It will not commit, push, or create a PR on its own.

Examples:
  CVE-2024-45338 --repo=https://github.com/openshift/hypershift
  --jira=OCPBUGS-12345
  --jira=OCPBUGS-12345 --repo=hypershift --algo=rta
  --jql="project = OCPBUGS AND labels = needs-cve-analysis ORDER BY created ASC"
